newsitem.title: FRANCE: French maize hits season's high, wheat retreats.
newsitem.headline: French maize hits season's high, wheat retreats.

text.p: French old-crop maize prices into Bordeaux reached the season's high on Tuesday amid sustained demand from the starch and animal feed industry, dealers said.
Support also came from expectations that mounting drought fears might spark more demand in the coming weeks to feed cattle normally raised on grass, they said.
Old- and new-crop wheat prices were easier on hopes that eagerly- awaited rainfall might hit France over the weekend.
Maize for April-June delivery into Bordeaux was quoted at 900 francs per tonne, excluding carrying charges, up five francs from Monday. But only small volumes were traded.
Fob Atlantic maize for April-September delivery was bid at 920 francs per tonne, up 10 francs from Monday.
Wheat for May delivery into Rouen was quoted at 920 francs per tonne, excluding carrying charges, down five.
Wheat for August-December delivery into Rouen was quoted at 925 francs per tonne, down 10 francs.
Milling wheat futures on MATIF were firmer, with the September 1997 expiry quoted at 931 francs per tonne, up eight francs on Monday. Total volume was 82 lots.

French domestic grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of each July/June crop year.
